_about: Mutation-test targets for this plugin. Each target names the file to mutate and
the test command that must notice a change (the fast suite that covers it).
Run with tools/mutator.py, or as part of tools/run_tests.sh.
min_kill_rate is the floor: below it the run fails, and a target that yields no
mutants at all fails too, so a mutation pass can never be green over nothing.
per_operator caps how many occurrences of each operator are mutated (determinism
and runtime); raise it for a deeper run via --max-rate/--only.
equivalent lists survivors that were PROVEN unobservable by applying the mutant
and diffing the target's full test output against the baseline (they are excluded
from the denominator, never counted as kills) — each names its (line, kind) and a
reason. exempt lists shipped sources deliberately not mutated, each with a reason;
policy_check's tests/no-gaps rule requires every source_globs match to be accounted
for here or be a target.

equivalent.reason: notify()'s guard redirects to /dev/null; 2>&1 -> 3>&1 only opens an unused fd3 and discards the same empty `command -v` output — proven identical by diffing the full test output
dry_run is only ever tested with [[ -n $dry_run ]], so the sentinel 1 vs 2 is indistinguishable — proven identical by diffing the full test output

notify()'s guard redirects to /dev/null; 2>&1 -> 3>&1 opens an unused fd3 and 2>&1 -> 2>&2 is a self-duplication no-op, both discarding the same empty `command -v` output — proven identical by diffing the full test output

inside `i = max(close + 1, i + 1)`: on this branch close >= i, so close+1 > i-1 and max() always returns close+1 — the i+1 -> i-1 change is unobservable, proven by diffing the full test output (identical rc and output)

subprocess timeout=120 vs 121s: no test (nor the suite) ever lets a command approach the timeout, so the value is unobservable — proven by applying the mutant and diffing the full test output (identical rc and output)
subprocess timeout=120 vs 121s: unobservable, no stubbed or real command approaches the timeout — proven by diffing the full test output (identical)
the error returncode sentinel 1 vs 2: every caller branches on `code != 0` / `code == 0`, so any non-zero value is indistinguishable — proven by diffing the full test output (identical)

exempt.reason: privileged installer (sudo/pkexec, /usr/local/bin); mutating it meaningfully needs a root harness, wiring is verified by review
